I live in North Carolina (US), near the center. It's actually very rare to find good, untouched areas around here due to the manner in which the cities have been expanding. Due to their ages and slow growth until recently, they expand outward and not upward, leading to a massively wide diameter of urban areas scattered all along the Piedmont (center region) It takes a good 30+ minute drive to actually start escaping the cities. More like 2 hours to start seeing untouched areas. Generally any "nature" expeditions becomes a day trip as a result, especially if you want to find the really remote areas.

Some of my favorite places for exploring include Hiddenite, NC (towards the mountains) and the beaches, especially on the north tip of Wrightsville beach island (mostly undisturbed, lots of bird and turtle nests) and some of the south (excellent area to catch tiny crabs). To be frank, I've never foraged out of need but just out of curiosity. I love looking for rocks, mushrooms with odd colors (I don't eat them), and little hidden "oases" where the illusion of complete wilderness can occur.
